title: 02 Displaying and comparing quantitative data: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 02 Displaying and comparing quantitative data: Visual Guide

1. Labels Or Ruler | the bridge from lesson 1 — the same twelve load times drawn once as equally spaced category labels and once as positions on a number line, with one value draggable from 30 to 300 s | a categorical axis carries order but no distance, so quantitative values need a ruler; text ordering even files 300 between 30 and 38

2. Binning A Histogram | 20 load times re-binned live as the bin width is dragged from 1 s to 40 s, with tappable bars reporting their interval and count | each bar is a numerical interval and its frequency, the counts always sum to 20, and bin width is a choice that can manufacture noise or erase the shape

3. Same Box, Different Data | two data sets with identical five-number summaries shown as a dot plot, a stem-and-leaf plot, a histogram and a box plot | dot plots and stem-and-leaf plots keep every individual value and the histogram keeps the shape, but the box plot condenses to five numbers and cannot tell a unimodal set from a bimodal one

4. Naming The Shape | a modality control (one peak, two peaks, flat) crossed with a slider that stretches the tail left or right, with live mean and median markers | shape is modality plus skew, skew is named for the tail and not the bulk, and the mean is dragged toward the tail while the median resists because it is a rank

5. Two Groups Compared | group A against a shiftable group B on one shared axis, with an added straggler, drawn as side-by-side box plots or as dot plots | comparing distributions means shape, center, spread and outliers on a shared scale, and a single extreme value moves the range and the mean while the median and IQR barely change
